info.title: QuanticData API
info.summary: Scrape, search, crawl, unlock, run collectors and build datasets — one host, one Bearer key, one JSON envelope.
info.description: This specification is generated from the application source (route handlers, auth middleware, billing config). Every endpoint answers the same envelope: `{"type":"response","message":"…","payload":{…}}` on success and `{"type":"error","message":"…","payload":{…}}` on failure. Data API calls are pay-per-success: a blocked page, a target 4xx/5xx, a timeout or an error on our side is never charged. The Web Unlocker is the exception: it spends prepaid GB on all the traffic it moves, blocked pages included (see its section). Billed responses carry `payload.usage` (`cost_usd`, `free_usd`, `paid_usd`, `balance`). Prices are not part of this document: see https://quanticdata.io/pricing/ and `GET /scraper/billing` for the prices that apply to your account.

tags.name: Web Unlocker
tags.description:
Replay any HTTP request through a residential or mobile exit under a real browser fingerprint, with retries on fresh exits, a headless browser for JavaScript challenges and one error catalogue; prepaid per GB.

One engine, three entry points. All three spend the same prepaid Web Unlocker GB, one balance per tier (`premium` = residential exits, `mobile` = mobile exits), bought on the Web Unlocker tab of the [plans page](https://app.quanticdata.io/plans?network=UNLOCK) and paid from the wallet balance, separate from the Data API free credit. Same targeting, same diagnostics, same errors.

### Which endpoint

| Entry point | Use it when | Endpoint |
|---|---|---|
| **REST API** | You can change your code: one JSON call in, one JSON answer out, no certificate to install. | `POST https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock` (the same call on the API host: `https://api.quanticdata.io/v1/scraper/unlock`) |
| **Proxy (CONNECT)** | You already have a scraper that speaks proxy: point it at the host and port with your unlocker user and password, and install the CA once. | `http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000` |
| **Direct mode** | Proxy without a certificate: send the request to `http://unlock/` through the proxy and name the target in the `x-qp-url` header. | `http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000`, then `http://unlock/` |

The REST call is `POST /scraper/unlock` below. The CA of the proxy is `GET /scraper/unlock/ca` (`https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca`). The [Web Unlocker page](https://app.quanticdata.io/unlock) of the dashboard shows the same three snippets filled with your own key, proxy user and password.

Many URLs at once go through the batch endpoints (see Batch). The price per GB of each tier, the pack sizes and the options that are switched on are published by `GET /public/unlock/offer` once the offer is public (`available: true`); `GET /public/unlock/status` publishes the latest canary run. Neither needs a key.

## Download a client

Two single-file clients cover the REST call and the batch endpoints. They have no dependency: download the file, put it next to your code and import it.

| Language | File | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| Node.js | [unlocker.mjs](https://quanticdata.io/docs/clients/unlocker.mjs) | Node 18 or later |
| Python | [unlocker.py](https://quanticdata.io/docs/clients/unlocker.py) | Python 3.9 or later |

**Node.js**

```javascript
import { Unlocker } from "./unlocker.mjs";

const client = new Unlocker({ apiKey: "qd_live_YOUR_API_KEY", retries: 2 });
const page = await client.unlock("https://example.com/", { country: "us", format: "markdown" });
console.log(page.status, page.tier_served, page.cost.bytes);
console.log(page.body.slice(0, 500));
```

**Python**

```python
from unlocker import Unlocker

client = Unlocker(api_key="qd_live_YOUR_API_KEY", retries=2)
page = client.unlock("https://example.com/", country="us", format="markdown")
print(page["status"], page["tier_served"], page["cost"]["bytes"])
print(page["body"][:500])
```

Both clients have `unlock(url, options)`, `batch(requests, options)`, `batchStatus(id)` and `batchCancel(id)` (also `batch_status` and `batch_cancel` in Python). Options are the REST fields in snake_case, `actions` and `cache_ttl` included. An error answer raises `UnlockerError` with `code`, `retryable`, `billed`, `hint`, `status` and `request_id`. `retries` (0 to 2, default 0) repeats a call whose error is retryable, after the `Retry-After` pause.

## Forward proxy

| | |
|---|---|
| Host | `unlock.quanticdata.io` |
| Port | `9000` (HTTP proxy) |
| Authentication | `Proxy-Authorization: Basic` with a **proxy user**: username `unlock-<12 hex>`, 32-character password. Your API key is not accepted by the proxy. |
| Targets | `http://` and `https://` URLs. HTTP/1.1 inside a CONNECT tunnel. |
| Limits | Request body up to 8 MB. Text responses up to 5 MB, binary up to 25 MB, or less with `x-qp-max-bytes`. At most 8 redirects are followed. One call, attempts and browser render included, fits in `x-qp-timeout` (default 60 s). |

### Proxy users

Create, rotate and delete proxy users on the [Web Unlocker page](https://app.quanticdata.io/unlock) of the dashboard, up to 20 per account; a proxy user can be created once the tier has GB. The password is shown when the user is created or rotated. The proxy caches a successful login for 60 seconds, so a rotated or deleted password can keep working for up to a minute. The same page builds ready-made proxy strings with the targeting below.

### Proxy (CONNECT)

The normal proxy setting of any HTTP client. The proxy re-issues your request itself, so it terminates TLS with its own certificate: download the CA once (`GET /scraper/unlock/ca`, saved as `unlocker-ca.pem` below) and trust it for the target host, or turn verification off (`curl -k`, `verify=False`).

<!-- unlocker-snippets:proxy -->
**curl**

```bash
# once: curl -o unlocker-ca.pem https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca
curl --proxy http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000 \
  --proxy-user "USER:PASS" \
  --cacert unlocker-ca.pem \
  https://example.com/
```

**Python (requests)**

```python
import requests

# once: download https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca as unlocker-ca.pem
proxy = "http://USER:PASS@unlock.quanticdata.io:9000"
r = requests.get(
    "https://example.com/",
    proxies={"http": proxy, "https": proxy},
    verify="unlocker-ca.pem",
    timeout=130,
)
print(r.status_code, r.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked", "ok"), r.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"))
print(r.text[:500])
```

**Node (undici)**

```javascript
import { fetch, ProxyAgent } from "undici";
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";

// once: download https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca as unlocker-ca.pem
const dispatcher = new ProxyAgent({
  uri: "http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000",
  token: "Basic " + Buffer.from("USER:PASS").toString("base64"),
  requestTls: { ca: readFileSync("unlocker-ca.pem") },
});
const res = await fetch("https://example.com/", { dispatcher });
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked") ?? "ok", res.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"));
console.log((await res.text()).slice(0, 500));
```

**PHP (curl)**

```php
<?php
// once: download https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca as unlocker-ca.pem
$ch = curl_init("https://example.com/");
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
  CURLOPT_PROXY => "http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000",
  CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD => "USER:PASS",
  CURLOPT_CAINFO => "unlocker-ca.pem",
  CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
  CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 130,
]);
$html = curl_exec($ch);
echo curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_HTTP_CODE), "\n", substr($html, 0, 500);
```

**Go**

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/tls"
	"crypto/x509"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"os"
)

func main() {
	// once: download https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock/ca as unlocker-ca.pem
	ca, _ := os.ReadFile("unlocker-ca.pem")
	pool := x509.NewCertPool()
	pool.AppendCertsFromPEM(ca)
	proxy, _ := url.Parse("http://USER:PASS@unlock.quanticdata.io:9000")
	client := &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{Proxy: http.ProxyURL(proxy), TLSClientConfig: &tls.Config{RootCAs: pool}}}
	res, err := client.Get("https://example.com/")
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)
	fmt.Println(res.StatusCode, res.Header.Get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked"), res.Header.Get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"), len(body))
}
```
<!-- /unlocker-snippets:proxy -->

### Direct mode

Nothing to install: address the proxy itself with plain HTTP at `http://unlock/` and put the target in `x-qp-url`. The proxy makes the TLS connection to the site. The method and body of your call are forwarded; `x-qp-method` overrides the method.

<!-- unlocker-snippets:direct -->
**curl**

```bash
curl --proxy http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000 \
  --proxy-user "USER:PASS" \
  -H "x-qp-url: https://example.com/" \
  http://unlock/
```

**Python (requests)**

```python
import requests

proxy = "http://USER:PASS@unlock.quanticdata.io:9000"
r = requests.get(
    "http://unlock/",
    proxies={"http": proxy},
    headers={"x-qp-url": "https://example.com/"},
    timeout=130,
)
print(r.status_code, r.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked", "ok"), r.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"))
print(r.text[:500])
```

**Node (undici)**

```javascript
import { fetch, ProxyAgent } from "undici";

const dispatcher = new ProxyAgent({
  uri: "http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000",
  token: "Basic " + Buffer.from("USER:PASS").toString("base64"),
});
const res = await fetch("http://unlock/", { dispatcher, headers: { "x-qp-url": "https://example.com/" } });
console.log(res.status, res.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked") ?? "ok", res.headers.get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"));
console.log((await res.text()).slice(0, 500));
```

**PHP (curl)**

```php
<?php
$ch = curl_init("http://unlock/");
curl_setopt_array($ch, [
  CURLOPT_PROXY => "http://unlock.quanticdata.io:9000",
  CURLOPT_PROXYUSERPWD => "USER:PASS",
  CURLOPT_HTTPHEADER => ["x-qp-url: https://example.com/"],
  CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER => true,
  CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 130,
]);
$html = curl_exec($ch);
echo curl_getinfo($ch, CURLINFO_HTTP_CODE), "\n", substr($html, 0, 500);
```

**Go**

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
)

func main() {
	proxy, _ := url.Parse("http://USER:PASS@unlock.quanticdata.io:9000")
	client := &http.Client{Transport: &http.Transport{Proxy: http.ProxyURL(proxy)}}
	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", "http://unlock/", nil)
	req.Header.Set("x-qp-url", "https://example.com/")
	res, err := client.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := io.ReadAll(res.Body)
	fmt.Println(res.StatusCode, res.Header.Get("x-qp-unlocker-blocked"), res.Header.Get("x-qp-unlocker-attempts"), len(body))
}
```
<!-- /unlocker-snippets:direct -->

A plain `http://` target works through the proxy as well, as an absolute-URI request (`GET http://example.com/ HTTP/1.1`), the way any client sends an `http://` URL through a proxy; no certificate involved.

### Targeting in the username

Append options to the proxy user, each as `-name-value`: `unlock-xxxxxxxxxxxx-country-us-session-abc123-ttl-30`. Unknown options are ignored.

| Option | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `country-xx` | 2-letter country code | Exit country. Without it, in order: the site's own country from its ccTLD (`.de`, `.fr`), then the country of your account, then US. |
| `state-<slug>`, `city-<slug>` | letters, digits, `_` (up to 32) | Exit region and city, e.g. `-state-new_york-city-new_york`. |
| `session-<id>` (or `sid-<id>`) | letters and digits (up to 32) | Keeps the same exit IP across requests and connections. |
| `ttl-<minutes>` | 3 to 1440 | How long that session's exit is kept; only together with `session`. |
| `profile-<name>` | `chrome` (default), `firefox`, `safari`, `safari_ios`, `edge`, `brave`, `mobile` | Browser fingerprint. Other values fall back to the default. |
| `mobile` | — | Mobile browser fingerprint on the same exits. It does not switch to the mobile network. |
| `tier-<name>` | `premium` (default), `mobile` | Product: exit network and GB balance the request is billed on. |
| `policy-<name>` | `browser` (default), `passthrough` | `passthrough` sends your own identity headers instead of the fingerprint's. |

### Control headers

Optional request headers, read by the proxy and removed before the request reaches the site (any other header, including other `x-qp-*` names, is forwarded). They work on every way of sending a request, inside a CONNECT tunnel too, and mirror the fields of the REST call. True values: `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`; false: `0`, `false`, `no`, `off`, `none` or empty. An invalid value is ignored and reported in `x-qp-warning`. The header names used by other unlocker services for the same options are accepted as aliases, so existing code keeps working: they are listed under Coming from another unlocker.

| Header | Values | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `x-qp-url` | absolute `http(s)` URL | Target in direct mode; wins over the request line. |
| `x-qp-method` | HTTP verb | Method sent to the site. |
| `x-qp-mode` | `auto` (default), `tls`, `browser` | Same as `mode` of the REST call: `auto` climbs from the TLS tier to the browser when blocked, `tls` never opens the browser, `browser` renders straight away. |
| `x-qp-max-bytes` | integer, at least 1024 | Same as `max_bytes`: cap on the bytes this call may move; over it the answer is 403 `max_bytes_exceeded`. |
| `x-qp-fail-on-block` | true/false | Same as `fail_on_block`: a refusal the site sent under its own status (403, 429, 503) answers 424 `target_blocked` instead of being relayed; a block page served as 2xx/3xx is 424 anyway (see Blocked pages). |
| `x-qp-timeout` | milliseconds, 1000 to 120000 | Same as `timeout_ms`: total budget of the call (default 60000), attempts and browser render included. |
| `x-qp-cache-ttl` | seconds, 0 to 86400 | Same as `cache_ttl`: an identical GET is answered from a stored copy younger than this (see Cache). 0 or absent: no cache. |
| `x-qp-country` (or `x-qp-geo`) | 2-letter code | Exit country for this request. |
| `x-qp-session` (or `x-qp-session-id`) | letters and digits (up to 32) | Exit session for this request. |
| `x-qp-rotation` | `sticky`, `rotating` | Session behaviour. |
| `x-qp-profile` (or `x-qp-tls-profile`) | profile name | Browser fingerprint. |
| `x-qp-keep-headers` | true/false | Send your own identity headers verbatim. |
| `x-qp-render` | `html` or true, `png`, false | `html`/true is `x-qp-mode: browser`; `png` returns a screenshot (GET/HEAD); false is `x-qp-mode: tls`. |
| `x-qp-auto-render` (or `x-qp-escalate`) | true/false | Deprecated, use `x-qp-mode`: false is `tls`, true is `auto`. |
| `x-qp-success-status` | comma-separated codes, 100 to 599 | Origin statuses relayed as success, never retried. |
| `x-qp-wait-for` (or `x-qp-wait-for-selector`) | CSS selector (up to 256) | Browser waits for this element before capturing. |
| `x-qp-wait-ms` (or `x-qp-wait`) | 0 to 15000 | Extra settle time in the browser. |
| `x-qp-return-cookies` | true | Return the site's cookie jar in `x-qp-cookies`. |

### Response headers

The site's status, headers and body are relayed (the body decompressed, `Set-Cookie` lines from every redirect kept), plus the same diagnostics the REST payload carries:

| Header | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x-qp-request-id` | Id of this exchange (`request_id` of the REST payload), to quote to support. |
| `x-qp-latency-ms` | Milliseconds from your request to the answer (`latency_ms`). |
| `x-qp-tier-served` | `tls` or `browser`: the tier that produced the answer (`tier_served`). |
| `x-qp-cost-bytes`, `x-qp-cost-usd` | Bytes moved for this call and what they cost at your tier's price per GB (`cost.bytes`, `cost.usd`). |
| `x-qp-attempt-log` | `attempt_log` as URL-encoded JSON: one entry per attempt with tier, profile, exit country, outcome, ms and bytes. |
| `x-qp-cache`, `x-qp-cached-at` | `hit`, `miss` or `off` (`cache` of the REST payload) and, on a hit, when the copy was stored (`cached_at`). |
| `x-qp-unlocker-attempts` | Attempts across every tier. |
| `x-qp-unlocker-profile` | Fingerprint that served the response. |
| `x-qp-session` | Exit session used. |
| `x-qp-country` | Exit country used. |
| `x-qp-final-url` | URL after redirects. |
| `x-qp-unlocker-rendered`, `x-qp-unlocker-escalated` | `1` when the headless browser served it, or was reached by escalation. |
| `x-qp-clearance` | `hit`, `miss`, `minted`, `stale` or `off`. |
| `x-qp-unlocker-blocked` | Block reason, when every attempt came back blocked (the status depends on how the site served the block, see Blocked pages). |
| `x-qp-block-class` | `js_challenge`, `captcha`, `access_denied`, `rate_limited`, `fingerprint`, `geo`, `timeout` or `unknown`. |
| `x-qp-vendor` | Anti-bot system, when recognised. |
| `x-qp-hint` | Suggestion when blocked, e.g. try the `mobile` tier. |
| `x-qp-origin-status` | The status the site really sent, when the proxy answered 424 `target_blocked` instead: a block page served as 2xx/3xx, or a refusal turned into 424 by `x-qp-fail-on-block`. |
| `x-qp-cookies` | URL-encoded JSON cookie jar, with `x-qp-return-cookies`. |
| `x-qp-ratelimit-limit`, `x-qp-ratelimit-remaining` | Requests per minute and what is left. |
| `x-qp-warning` | A control header or option that was ignored, and why. |

### Modes, retries and sessions

In `auto` mode (the default) a GET, HEAD or OPTIONS is retried up to three times on a new exit with a different fingerprint, then escalated to a headless browser that can start in parallel when the first attempts come back blocked; `tier_served` (or `x-qp-tier-served`) says which tier produced the answer. `tls` never opens the browser and returns the block page as-is; `browser` renders straight away. Everything fits in the call's total budget (`timeout_ms` / `x-qp-timeout`, default 60 s): a budget that runs out is a 504 `timeout`. Any other method gets exactly one attempt and no browser fallback: a response means the site saw the request, and replaying a POST could submit it twice. With a `session` in the username the exit cannot change, so there is one normal attempt; the browser fallback still runs.

### Browser actions

`actions` (REST call only) is an ordered list of up to 20 interactions the browser runs before the page is captured: click an element or a text, type into a field, scroll, wait. Actions force the browser tier, so they work on GET and HEAD only, and `mode: "tls"` together with `actions` is a 400 `bad_request`. The shapes are listed in the request body of `POST /scraper/unlock`. An action that cannot run ends the call with 422 `action_failed`, and the message names it: `Action 2 failed ({"waitForSelector":".results"}): nothing on the page matched it within 15000 ms`. An action marked `optional: true` is skipped instead, and the call goes on.

### Cache

`cache_ttl` (REST) or `x-qp-cache-ttl` (proxy) is a number of seconds from 0 to 86400; 0, the default, is off. A GET that the site answered 2xx and that was not blocked is kept for your account for that long. A later call with the same URL, mode, format, country, tier, render kind and actions is answered from the copy. That answer says `cache: "hit"` and `cached_at` (`x-qp-cache` and `x-qp-cached-at` on the proxy), with `attempts: 0` and one `attempt_log` entry of tier `cache`; `tier_served` is the tier that produced the stored page. A hit moves no bytes and costs nothing: `cost` is `{"bytes": 0, "usd": 0, "billed": false}`. The cache is best effort: a copy can be dropped before its time, and a page over 5 MB is not kept.

### Billing and limits

The price per GB of each tier is on the [plans page](https://app.quanticdata.io/plans?network=UNLOCK) of the dashboard and, when the offer is published, in `GET /public/unlock/offer`. Every byte the exit network carries for your request is debited from the tier's prepaid GB: retries, blocked pages, failed attempts and the browser's page load included (request bodies and response bodies; headers are not counted). 1 GB = 10^9 bytes. 429 answers and requests refused before they ran are not billed, and a cache hit moves no bytes. When `pay_per_success` of `GET /public/unlock/offer` is true, a blocked page or a failed call debits nothing on the REST call and in a batch; the forward proxy is metered on every byte either way. `max_bytes` / `x-qp-max-bytes` caps what one call may move. The balance is checked when the proxy logs you in, so a session can run for up to a minute past the end of the GB. Requests per minute and concurrent requests follow the account's Data API tier (see Rate limits and tiers).

## Batch

Up to 100 URLs in one asynchronous job. `POST /scraper/unlock/batch` takes the list and answers 202 with a `batch_id` at once. `GET /scraper/unlock/batch/{batch_id}` returns the progress and one result per item. `DELETE /scraper/unlock/batch/{batch_id}` cancels the items that have not started. Each item is a REST call: any field of `POST /scraper/unlock` can be set per item, or once for all of them in `defaults`. `concurrency` (1 to 5, default 3) is how many items run at the same time. With `webhook_url` the finished batch is also sent to your server in one POST. Results are kept for one hour after the batch ends.

Billing: a batch spends the same prepaid GB, and every item is metered like a single call. The tier needs usable GB when the batch starts, otherwise the answer is 402 `no_credit`.

## Errors

One catalogue for the REST call and the proxy. A REST error is the usual envelope, `{"type":"error","message":"…","payload":{…}}`, where `payload` carries `code`, `retryable`, `billed`, `hint` and `doc_url` (this section) plus the details named below; the code is repeated in the `x-qp-unlocker` header and retryable answers carry `Retry-After` with a suggested pause. The proxy answers the same status and JSON body with the same headers; a CONNECT that is refused gets no body, only the status line plus `X-Qp-Unlocker` (code) and, for 402, `X-Qp-Unlocker-Message` (curl prints "Received HTTP code 402 from proxy after CONNECT").

### Unlock errors

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Billed | When | What to do |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bad_request` | 400 | no | no | A parameter is invalid; `message` names it and the rule it broke. | Fix the parameter named in the message and send the request again. |
| `unauthorized` | 401 | no | no | API key missing, wrong or disabled. On the proxy: 407 with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic`, only for a missing or wrong proxy user. | Use the API key from the dashboard (REST) or the unlocker proxy user and password (proxy). |
| `no_credit` | 402 | no | no | The tier has no usable GB: never bought, used up or expired. `payload.reason` says which; `payload.buy_url` is the page to buy GB. | Buy GB from the dashboard, then retry with the same key or proxy user. |
| `target_forbidden` | 403 | no | no | Private, reserved or internal address. | The unlocker only fetches public hosts. |
| `target_denied` | 403 | no | no | A destination the unlocker does not serve (banking, payments, login providers, crypto sites). | Pick another target; this one is on the deny list. |
| `no_exit_pool` | 403 | no | no | The account has no exit pool for the tier (e.g. `mobile` without a mobile sub-user); `payload.tier` names it. On the proxy the same answer is 503 (see Proxy-only answers). | Buy GB on that tier so its pool is set up, or use `tier: "premium"`; retry once the pool exists. |
| `max_bytes_exceeded` | 403 | no | yes | The bytes moved went over `max_bytes`; `payload.usage` and `payload.cost` say how many. | Raise `max_bytes`, or leave it out to accept the full page. |
| `action_failed` | 422 | no | no | REST call with `actions`: the page loaded but one of the actions could not run, for example its selector matched nothing in time. `message` names the action by its position and shape and says why. | Check the selector or the text of that action, or mark it `optional` if the page may not have it. |
| `target_blocked` | 424 | yes | yes | The target refused every attempt and you asked `fail_on_block` (REST) or `x-qp-fail-on-block` (proxy), or, on the proxy, the site served its block page under a 2xx/3xx status; `payload` carries `status`, `blockReason`, `blockClass`, `vendor`, `attempts`, `attempt_log`, `usage` and `cost`. | Retry with `mode: "browser"`, another country, or a sticky session; drop `fail_on_block` to receive the blocked page as a 200. |
| `rate_limited` | 429 | yes | no | Requests per minute or concurrent requests of the account's tier. | Wait for `Retry-After` seconds, lower your concurrency, or move to a plan with a higher limit. |
| `render_failed` | 503 | yes | no | The browser could not load the page. | Retry; if it keeps failing use `mode: "tls"` or a longer `timeout_ms`. |
| `upstream_failed` | 503 | yes | no | The exit or the target could not be reached. | Retry: the next attempt runs on a fresh exit. |
| `service_unavailable` | 503 | yes | no | The engine or the API is not answering (on the proxy: 503, never 407). | Retry in a few seconds. |
| `timeout` | 504 | yes | no | `timeout_ms` ran out before a response. | Raise `timeout_ms` (up to 120000) or use `mode: "tls"` for a faster first answer. |
| `internal_error` | 500 | yes | no | An error on our side. | Retry; if it persists contact support with the `request_id`. |

### Proxy-only answers

Answers only the forward proxy gives (the REST call has no equivalent), same JSON body and `x-qp-unlocker` header as the catalogue:

| Code | HTTP | Retryable | Billed | When |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `proxy_auth_required` | 407 | no | no | No `Proxy-Authorization` header. Comes with `Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="Web Unlocker"`. |
| `proxy_auth_invalid` | 407 | no | no | Wrong proxy user or password. |
| `not_a_proxy_request` | 400 | no | no | A request that is neither proxy-shaped (CONNECT, or an absolute URI) nor direct mode (`x-qp-url`). |
| `body_too_large` | 413 | no | no | Request body over 8 MB. |
| `too_many_connections` | 429 | yes | no | More concurrent connections than the account's tier allows; `Retry-After` says when to retry. |
| `sensitive_rate_limited` | 429 | yes | no | Non-GET requests to login-like paths over the limit; `Retry-After`. |
| `auth_rate_limited` | 429 | yes | no | More than 30 failed logins per minute from one IP; `Retry-After`. |
| `no_exit_pool` | 503 | no, until a pool exists | no | The account has no exit pool for the tier (e.g. `tier-mobile` without a mobile sub-user). The REST call answers 403 `no_exit_pool` for the same situation. |

### Blocked pages

On the REST call a page that is still blocked after every attempt is not an error unless you ask for one: the answer is 200 with `blocked: true`, `blockClass`, `vendor` and `hint`, and the block page is in `body` for inspection; `fail_on_block: true` turns it into 424 `target_blocked`. On the proxy the answer depends on how the site served the block. A block page the site served under a 2xx/3xx status is answered 424 `target_blocked` straight away, with the site's body and the headers `x-qp-unlocker: target_blocked`, `x-qp-origin-status` (the status the site sent), `x-qp-unlocker-blocked`, `x-qp-block-class` and `x-qp-vendor`. A refusal the site sent under its own status (403, 429, 503) is relayed with that status and the same diagnostic headers, and becomes 424 only with `x-qp-fail-on-block: 1`. Captchas: when the service has the captcha solver enabled (`captcha_solver` of `GET /public/unlock/offer`), DataDome and AWS WAF challenges are handed to it, and `attempt_log` shows that step as a `solver` entry. Any other interactive captcha is returned as `blockClass: "captcha"`.

### Reading a block: vendor and blockClass

When an attempt meets a wall, the engine names the system it recognised in `vendor` and the kind of stop in `blockClass`. Both are on the REST answer when `blocked` is `true`, on the entries of `attempt_log`, on each result of a batch, and on the proxy as the headers `x-qp-vendor` and `x-qp-block-class`.

| `vendor` | System | What the block of that system looks like |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cloudflare` | Cloudflare | 403 with "Just a moment..." and the header `cf-mitigated: challenge`; errors 1020, 1015, 1010, 1009 |
| `datadome` | DataDome | 403 with "Please enable JS and disable any ad blocker" and a script from `captcha-delivery.com` |
| `akamai` | Akamai Bot Manager | 403 "Access Denied ... Reference #18..." |
| `perimeterx` | PerimeterX (HUMAN) | 403 with "Press & Hold to confirm you are a human"; on API calls a JSON body with `appId` |
| `kasada` | Kasada | 429 on the first request, with an almost empty page that loads `ips.js` |
| `imperva` | Imperva (Incapsula) | "Pardon Our Interruption" or "Request unsuccessful. Incapsula incident ID", often with status 200 |
| `shape` | F5 (BIG-IP, Shape) | "Request Rejected ... Your support ID is", often with status 200 |
| `awswaf` | AWS WAF | 202 (Challenge) or 405 (CAPTCHA), with the header `x-amzn-waf-action` |
| `amazon`, `google`, `reddit`, `yandex` | The site's own wall | The page that site shows to automated traffic |
| `hcaptcha`, `recaptcha` | A captcha widget | An interactive captcha on the page |
| `unknown` | Not recognised | Read `blockReason` and the body |

| `blockClass` | What stopped the call | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `js_challenge` | A check that a real browser clears by running a script | Leave `mode` on `auto`, or use `browser`. With `mode: "tls"` no browser is opened |
| `captcha` | The page asks a person: a puzzle, a slider, press and hold | Retry later or from another `country`. See the captcha rule above |
| `access_denied` | A flat refusal, with no challenge offered | Retry; try another `country` or the mobile tier |
| `rate_limited` | A plain 429 | Slow down or spread the calls. Do not pin one session |
| `fingerprint` | The client itself was judged automated | Leave `mode` on `auto`: the browser tier is the next step |
| `geo` | The site does not serve the country of the exit | Set `country` to one the site serves |
| `timeout` | The site or the exit never answered | Retry |
| `unknown` | Not classified | Read `blockReason` and the body |

Two things worth knowing when you read the answer:

- The status code of the site is not proof. Imperva and F5 often serve their block page with status 200, and Kasada answers a new visitor with 429 before any rate was exceeded. `blocked` is the field to trust; `fail_on_block: true` turns a blocked answer into 424 `target_blocked`.
- `clearance` says what happened to the session of that site. `minted`: this call passed the site's check and the session was kept. `hit`: this call reused a kept session, so no new check was run. `stale`: a kept session was refused and dropped. `miss`: there was none. The first call to a protected site is the slow one; the next calls from the same account reuse the session until the site asks again.

<!-- other-unlockers -->

## Coming from another unlocker

Code written for another unlocker needs a new host, port and credentials. After that, most options keep working or need one rename: the proxy already reads several header names such code sends, and the rest map one to one to ours.

### Our names

| Option | REST field | Proxy header | Proxy username |
|---|---|---|---|
| Country | `country` | `x-qp-country` | `-country-xx` |
| Session | `session_id` | `x-qp-session` | `-session-<id>` |
| Render | `mode: "browser"`; `render: "png"` for a screenshot | `x-qp-mode: browser`; `x-qp-render: png` |  |
| Device | `mobile: true` or `tls_profile` | `x-qp-profile` | `-mobile`, `-profile-<name>` |
| Custom success codes | `success_status_codes` | `x-qp-success-status` |  |
| Markdown | `format: "markdown"` |  |  |
| Wait for an element | `wait_for_selector` | `x-qp-wait-for` |  |
| Timeout | `timeout_ms` | `x-qp-timeout` |  |

tags.name: Proxies
tags.description:
List your proxy plans, generate endpoint strings, manage IP whitelists, and get a new IP on demand. Limits: `generate` returns 1 to 10000 lines per call; the number of whitelisted IPs per plan is the plan's `whitelistSlots`; `ip-info` answers from a 24-hour cache per IP, and new lookups share a daily cap (503 with `Retry-After` when it is reached). Every call also counts in the hourly window of your API key (see Rate limits and tiers).

**New IP on demand.** A rotating string changes IP on every request. A sticky string keeps one IP for its session (`sessionTime` in `generate`). On Residential Basic and Datacenter traffic plans you can restart a sticky session at any time: the same string leaves from a new IP on its next request, so a saved anti-detect profile or a script keeps its proxy settings. Call `POST /public/proxies/{orderId}/rotate` with your API key, or create a rotation link: a URL with no key and no header that anti-detect browsers and scripts can call directly.

| Plan type (`planType`) | Rotating strings | Sticky strings | New IP on demand |
|---|---|---|---|
| `residentialbasic`, `datacentertraffic` | New IP per request | Same IP for `sessionTime` | `rotate` or a rotation link: same string, new IP |
| `residentialpremium`, `resiprivate`, `mobile_v2`, `mobile`, `ipv6` | New IP per request | Same IP for `sessionTime` | Request a new sticky string with `generate` |
| `datacenter` | Assigned by the gateway | Assigned by the gateway | Not applicable |
| `isp`, `isppremium` | Static IPs | Static IPs | Not applicable: dedicated static IPs |

**Super sticky and UDP.** On Residential Premium and Mobile, `superSticky: true` in `generate` keeps one IP per string with no session timer, for as long as the device behind it stays online. On Residential Basic, `udp: true` with `protocol: "socks5"` adds UDP relay (SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE) to the strings, rotating or sticky.

Build proxy strings with `generate` and use them as returned; do not edit them by hand.

Buy IPv6 speed plans through the API, paid from the wallet balance only (0% VAT; the balance is topped up in the dashboard): traffic is not metered, the port speed is the cap. Limits per account, on top of the hourly window of the API key: 300 grid reads and 300 quotes an hour, 20 purchase requests an hour, 120 order reads an hour shared by the order list and the single order. Over the account cap: 429 `RATE_LIMITED` with `retryAfter` (seconds) and `Retry-After`.

x-rate-limits.description: Per API key. Two windows apply: the tier's requests/minute (the tier table → rateLimitPerMin) and an hourly window of max(1000, rateLimitPerMin × 60). Envelope.description: Success envelope shared by every endpoint.

pagination.description: Empty `{}` unless the endpoint pages (SERP mirrors its own pagination here).

ErrorEnvelope.description: Error envelope. `payload` is present only when the error carries structured detail (codes, balances, limits). `escalation` is present only on a 402 that asks to talk to the team instead of paying (see `ContactEscalation`).

Usage.description: What the call cost. Present only on billed calls (absent when billing is off for the account or the key is an admin key).

cost_usd.description: Total cost of the call, USD, after the tier discount.

free_usd.description: Portion covered by the monthly free allowance.

balance.description: Wallet balance after the debit, present only when the wallet was touched.

Geo.description: Echo of the geo-targeting the call used.

GeoValue.description: Country code or place name: letters, digits, spaces, dots, hyphens, underscores; max 56 characters. `all` means no targeting.

ExtractSchema.description: Structured-extraction schema: field name → CSS selector, or an object with `selector`, optional `attr` (attribute to read instead of text) and `all` (true = every match as an array).

oneOf.description: CSS selector; the element's text is returned.

PageAction.description: One interaction before capture (render tier). Shapes are enforced by the scraper service; at most 20 actions, each a plain object. A `fetchResource` action must be last: the matching network response becomes the result body.

ForwardHeaders.description: Extra headers replayed to the target. Either a JSON object (name → value) or a raw `Header: Value` block, one per line (lines starting with `//` or `#` are ignored). Max 32 headers, names must be RFC 7230 tokens, values ≤ 4096 characters; hop-by-hop and framing headers (host, content-length, transfer-encoding, connection, …) are rejected.

PageMetadata.description: Meta/OpenGraph data of an HTML page (keys depend on what the page declares).

appState.description: The page's own hydration state (Next/Nuxt/JSON islands), present only when `app_state` was requested.

ExtractResult.description: Payload of a scrape. Optional fields appear only when requested (`data`, `links`, `screenshot`, `xhr`, `formats`, `contents`, `chunks`, `highlights`, `ai`).

content.description: The page in the requested format (empty in `mode: summary`).

bytes.description: Proxy bandwidth the fetch used — the metered part of the price.

engine.description: Engine that actually served the page; decides between the `extract` and `extract_render` price.

escalated.description: True when `engine: auto` escalated from the TLS tier to the browser.

blockReason.description: Present when the final page was an anti-bot block (the call is then not charged).

jsLikely.description: Content came out near-empty but the HTML is a JS app shell: retry with `render: true`.

resource.description: The network response captured by a `fetchResource` action; its body is `content`.

data.description: Values of the `extract` schema (or of the `presetId` parser).

documentKind.description: Set when the URL was a binary document converted to text (pdf, docx, xlsx, csv).

ai.description: AI extraction result (`ai_prompt`/`ai_schema`): `data`, `truncated`, `model`, `usage`; or `error` when the model step failed (the scrape itself still succeeded).

link.description: The result URL. On Google results it can be Google's click address (`https://www.google.com/url?…`) instead of the site's own URL: it opens the result in a browser, and `redirect_link` carries the same address.

redirect_link.description: Google's click address for the result (`https://www.google.com/url?…`) when Google links the result through one, otherwise `null`.

SerpResult.description: Search result in the common SERP-API JSON shape (drop-in for most existing SERP clients). Vertical arrays are always present (empty when the vertical did not apply); the single-object verticals (`place_results`, `product_results`, `trends`, `trending`, `knowledge_graph`, …) are null when absent.

search_url.description: The engine URL that was searched, with the engine's own parameters only.

from_cache.description: Served from the 24h result cache — identical requests are free.

path.description: Winning fetch tier. `http` bills the `serp` price; anything else bills `serp_render` (Google only).

served_device.description: Google: the device the returned page was served for, read from the page itself (`search_parameters.device` is the device you asked for). Web, news and videos never return the other device's page: if Google keeps serving it, the call ends with 429 `device-mismatch`, unbilled, and can be retried. Absent where the source is not a results page (autocomplete, Maps, place details, trends, reviews).

served_platform.description: Google web, news and videos: the device the page was fetched as (`android` for `mobile`, `ios` and `android`; `desktop`).

served_browser.description: Google web, news and videos: the browser the page was fetched as (`edge`).

empty_reason.description: Present when a Success carries no results, and says why: `no_results` = the engine's own "no results" page (Google's "did not match any documents"; Bing's "There are no results", taken only from a browser attempt, never from the HTTP tier alone). A zero-result page without a reason never leaves as a Success for Google search or Bing web search: it is a 429 (`empty-soft-throttle`, `bing-decoy`, `bing-no-results`), unbilled, that you can retry.

html.description: Full page HTML, only with `include_html: true`.

groups.description: Path tree with counts (depth 2), only with `group_by: path`.

JobStarted.description: Answer of a POST that started an async job.

statusUrl.description: Dashboard-host path to poll (prefix it with the app host, or call the same path on the API host without `/api`).

usage.description: The up-front charge on the requested volume; the unfetched share is refunded when the job settles.

nextCursor.description: Pass as `since` on the next poll to receive only newer pages.

hasMore.description: Finished pages beyond `nextCursor` were withheld (byte budget or cursor).

content.description: Only with `include_content=true` and not in `mode: summary`.

contentLength.description: Summary mode: characters of the converted content.

blockReason.description: Anti-bot block: the URL counts as failed and is refunded.

contentTruncated.description: The job hit its memory budget; later items carry metadata only.

organic.description: Merged, de-duplicated, re-ranked across pages (from `since` onwards).

UnlockResult.description: The target's response, replayed. `bodyBase64` is always present and is the raw page; `body` only when the content type is text-like (html, xml, text, json, javascript), in the `format` asked for HTML pages. `blocked: true` means every tier came back with a challenge or refusal and the payload is that page, for inspection.

request_id.description: Id of this exchange, the same value as the `x-qp-request-id` header; quote it to support.

body.description: The response as text, in the `format` asked (`html`, `markdown`, `text`) when the page is HTML; absent for binary content.

bodyBase64.description: The raw response body, base64, always present.

attempts.description: Number of attempts across every tier (the detail is in `attempt_log`); 0 when the answer came from the cache.

blocked.description: Every tier came back with a challenge or refusal; the payload is that page, for inspection.

vendor.description: Anti-bot system, when recognised: `cloudflare`, `datadome`, `akamai`, `perimeterx`, `kasada`, `imperva`, `shape` (F5), `awswaf`, `amazon`, `google`, `reddit`, `yandex`, `hcaptcha`, `recaptcha` or `unknown`. See "Reading a block" in the Web Unlocker guide.

hint.description: Suggestion when blocked, e.g. try the `mobile` tier.

clearance.description: What the engine did with its per-tenant clearance cache.

cookies.description: Full cookie jar, only with `returnCookies: true`.

rendered.description: The headless browser produced the answer.

escalated.description: The browser was reached by escalation after blocked TLS attempts.

tier_served.description: The tier that produced the answer (same as the `x-qp-tier-served` header). On a cache hit: the tier that produced the stored page.

latency_ms.description: Milliseconds from the request to the answer, every attempt included (same as `x-qp-latency-ms`).

cache.description: `hit`: answered from the cache, no bytes moved; `miss`: `cache_ttl` was set and the page was fetched; `off`: no `cache_ttl`. Same as the `x-qp-cache` header.

cached_at.description: On a hit: when the copy was stored. Same as the `x-qp-cached-at` header.

attempt_log.description: One entry per attempt, in order (same data as the `x-qp-attempt-log` header).

usage.description: Unlocker usage is metered in bytes against the tier's prepaid GB, not the wallet.

bytes.description: Bytes the exit network moved for this call: every attempt and tier, not only the body returned.

unlock_gb_remaining.description: GB left on the tier after this call.

unlock_gb_purchased.description: GB bought on the tier, lifetime of the current package.

data.description: The extracted JSON (shape follows the task).

steps.description: One entry per page the agent fetched.

usage.description: LLM token usage (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`) merged with the billing block (`cost_usd`, `free_usd`, `paid_usd`).

AiFinderResult.description: Shared shape of the AI Places and AI Shopping finders.

enriched.description: Places finder only: knowledge-panel lookups performed.

usage.description: LLM token usage merged with the billing block.

blockers.description: Checks whose failure caps the overall (blocked crawler, noindex, no text).

access.description: robots.txt verdict per AI crawler, Content-Signal, sitemaps, llms.txt, the fetch that identified itself as an AI crawler.

content.description: No-JS vs rendered view, readability metrics.

structure.description: JSON-LD types, entities, author, dates, heading outline.

retrievability.description: Google rank for the page's own H1 question and index status (2 SERPs), unless `no_retrieval`.

citations.description: Only with `queries`: `rows` (one per query × engine: cited / mentioned / rank / error), `usage`, share of voice.

offsite.description: Only with `offsite: true`: brand presence per platform.

render.description: Rendered view, or `{error}` when the render pass was skipped or failed (then the call bills the plain scrape price).

CollectorCatalogEntry.description: One collector. `input_schema` is a JSON Schema object (what to POST to `run_url`); `output_schema.fields` lists the columns of every delivered row.

unit.description: What one billed result is (place, review, job, …).

your_usd.description: List price × your tier discount — what you pay per delivered result.

price_key.description: The the price list key (`collector_<slug>`, or `collector_result` as fallback).

min_billable_results.description: Floor in units for a run that delivers anything; 0 = pure per-row.

max_results.description: Hard cap on rows per run.

input_schema.description: JSON Schema (type object, properties, required, additionalProperties: false).

tldr.description: One line on what the release changes for you. Optional: present on recent releases only.

partial.description: The run stopped before `max_results` (deadline, a page failed, …).

error_kind.description: `input` = retrying the same input cannot help (HTTP 422).

dropped.description: Lead collectors only: rows withheld by the removal list, your exclusion list or because already delivered to you.

results.description: Delivered rows (columns per `output_schema`). Absent in list views.

deduplicated.description: An identical run inside the dedup window was served instead of starting a new one — nothing new was charged.

DatasetSummary.description: One row of the dataset list.

costUsd.description: Real cost once settled (budget charge minus refund); null while running.

stored.description: Rows are stored and the run can be reopened/exported.

DatasetJob.description: Live job view (from the service) or the stored view of a finished run (`source: storage`, no progress/steps).

parser.description: Ready to pass as `extract` on any later scrape of this layout.

coverage.description: Fraction of requested fields that produced a value (0–1). 0 = not charged.

ProxyPlan.description: One proxy service on the account. `orderId` is what the generate and whitelist endpoints take.

sessionTime.description: Sticky session minutes of the strings; `null` for super sticky strings on Residential Premium and Mobile V2, which have no timer.

superSticky.description: `true` when the strings were built as super sticky sessions (no session timer).

udp.description: `true` when the strings carry the UDP option (Residential Basic, SOCKS5).

proxies.description: Ready-to-use proxy strings in the requested `format` (credentials included).

rotatingProxy.description: Plans that expose a single rotating endpoint.

IpInfo.description: Location and network of an IP, from ipinfo.io. Text the source does not give is an empty string.

ip.description: The address looked up, in canonical form.

regionCode.description: Always an empty string: the source gives no region code. Kept so existing clients keep working; use `region`.

lat.description: Latitude of the city area, never of a street.

lon.description: Longitude of the city area, never of a street.

isp.description: Network operator registered for the ASN.

as.description: ASN and operator, e.g. `AS15169 Google LLC`.

by_type.description: Requests per query type (extract, google, bing, map, crawl, batch, unlock, ai, …).

billed_usd.description: Wallet part of the spend (total − free).

billed.description: Whether this key's calls are charged (false for admin keys or when billing is off).

free_tier_blocked_reason.description: Why the allowance is 0; absent when conceded. `disposable_email`: the account's email address is disposable. `first_order_required`: on this account the free allowance starts with the first paid order.

prices_usd.description: The live price list with your tier discount applied — keyed like the price list.

PremiumIspPool.description: A ready Premium ISP pool: dedicated static IPs of one country, built for one category of sites. 30-day plans. `available` says whether the pool can be bought now; `maxQuantity` is the most IPs one order can take now (at most 200, lower when the pool is short of IPs). A pool with `subnet: true` sells a whole /24 instead: 256 dedicated IPs in one block, one subnet per order (`quantity` must be 256).

id.description: Pool id, `premium-<country>-<category>`, ending in `-subnet` for a whole /24. Use it as `poolId`.

maxQuantity.description: Most IPs one order can take now: at most 200, lower when the pool is short of IPs.

subnet.description: True for a whole /24 subnet: 256 IPs per order, `minQuantity` = `maxQuantity` = 256.

stock.description: IPs in stock now (a subnet takes 256); null when not reported.

replacementWithin24hOnRequest.description: IPs blocked by a site of the pool's category can be replaced within 24 hours of purchase, on request to support (not through the API). False for subnets.

subnetsOnRequest.description: Whole /24 subnets of this pool can be arranged with support. False on a subnet pool, which is bought through the API.

PremiumIspCityCatalog.description: City plans of one type: plan lengths with their price per IP, and the countries and cities with the IPs in stock. Served from a cache up to `maxAgeSeconds` old; the purchase reads stock again.

perIpPrice.description: Price per IP for the length, before quantity ranges, USD.

ranges.description: Price per IP by quantity range.

price.description: Price per IP in the range, USD.

replacementPrice.description: Price of one paid IP swap bought with the plan, USD.

carrierFeePerIp.description: Extra per IP when you pick a carrier (`asn`), USD.

maxReplacements.description: Paid IP swaps you can buy with one plan.

paidSwapPrice.description: USD for one IP swap bought after the purchase, from the plan page or `POST .../replacements` with `pay: true`; flat for this type.

siteCheck.description: The optional site test (`siteCheck` on the selection) is offered for this type.

guarantees.description: What every IP of a new plan comes with right now. `autoReplace`: free auto-replace, an IP that stays offline for more than 30 minutes is replaced by itself, same city, same login and password, without using an IP swap; the customer can switch it off for a plan on its dashboard page. `freshIps`: IPs never assigned to your account before, where available. stock.description: IPs in stock in the country; null when not reported.

asn.description: Carrier ASN. Pass it as `asn` to pin the carrier.

PremiumIspSelection.description: What to buy. A pool (`product: pool`) or a city plan (`product: city`).

type.description: City plans only. `fraud-score-0`: every IP is checked for a fraud score of 0 before delivery.

length.description: City plans only; the lengths on sale are listed by the catalog.

location.description: City plans only: a `location` from the catalog, e.g. `United States - New York City`. Or just the country name from the catalog (e.g. `United States`) for IPs from any city in that country — full-country stock, and it always uses any carrier (no `asn`).

asn.description: City plans only: carrier ASN from `GET /public/premium-isp/cities/carriers`; null = any carrier. Not allowed when `location` is a country name (any city).

ispNameCheck.description: City plans only. Deprecated and currently ignored: this free beta is turned off, so the flag has no effect and no IPs are filtered — leave it out. (When on, it delivered only IPs an IP-lookup database lists under an internet provider.)

siteCheck.description: City plans only, optional. A site test before delivery: every IP must open `url` and answer `expectedStatus` (default 200); IPs that fail are not assigned. Fewer IPs qualify, so delivery can take longer, and when none passes the order fails and is refunded to the balance by itself. A swapped IP is not tested again. url.description: A full http or https address with a public host name, no credentials.

replacements.description: City plans only: paid IP swaps bought with the plan (they cannot be added later). A swap changes a working IP, for example one a site blocks; an IP that goes offline is replaced free by auto-replace.

quantity.description: Number of IPs, within the length's or pool's minQuantity/maxQuantity: exactly 256 for a subnet pool.

PremiumIspQuote.description: Server-side price of a selection. Nothing is reserved (`reserved: false`).

subnet.description: Pools only: true for a whole /24 subnet (256 IPs).

city.description: `Any city` when the whole country was chosen.

anyCity.description: True when the plan is for any city in the country (full-country stock, no carrier).

ispNameCheck.description: Deprecated: the ISP name check beta is off, so this is always false.

carrierFeePerIp.description: Carrier fee per IP, USD; charged at purchase and at every renewal of the plan.

total.description: Amount charged to the balance, USD.

PremiumIspOrder.description: A Premium ISP order, from our records.

selection.description: What was bought: the pool (`poolId`, `name`) or the city pick (`type`, `length`, `location`, `city`, `country`, `asn`, `carrierName`, `udp`, `replacements`).

region.description: Same value as `region` in `GET /public/proxies`: the pool id, `premium-isp-city` or `premium-isp-city-fraud-score-0`.

replacements.description: City plans: paid IP swaps bought, used, being confirmed and left; `offline` lists the IPs that the network marks offline right now.

ip.description: The IP address that the network marks offline.

pending.description: `true` when the free replacement of this IP is already being confirmed: do not send it again.

PremiumIspLines.description: Proxy lines of an active order, read live.

terms.description: Terms in days that exist in the grid.

planName.description: The name the order and the invoice carry, e.g. `IPv6 Unlimited · 200 Mbps · 7 days`.

onRequest.description: The special plan with no price in the grid.

total.description: What the balance is charged, USD.

sufficientBalance.description: Whether the caller's balance covers `total`; null when the balance is not known.

Ipv6Order.description: An IPv6 speed order, from our records (dashboard and API purchases alike).

status.description: `refunded`: not delivered, the amount is back on the balance. `disabled`: switched off by support.

amount.description: List price in USD, before any coupon. Purchases from the balance add 0% VAT.

duration.description: Days the plan stays active after purchase.

whitelistSlots.description: IPs you can whitelist for IP authentication.

region.description: `Global` unless the plan is tied to a region.

speed.description: Speed tier in Mbps where the plan has one, else 0.

proxyType.description: Product family. For the exact plan type use `planType` from `GET /public/proxies`.

id.description: For `PROXY` orders, the `orderId` of the generate and whitelist endpoints.

plan.description: The plan bought; null on orders without a catalog plan (top-ups, plans configured at checkout).

region.description: Region label of the plan (`Global` when none), with the same values as `proxy.region`.

proxy.description: The proxy plan created by the order; null until it is delivered and on orders that are not proxies.

region.description: Region label of the plan (`Global` when none). Premium ISP city plans report `premium-isp-city`, or `premium-isp-city-fraud-score-0` for Fraud score 0 plans, as `GET /public/proxies` does.

balance.description: Wallet balance, USD. Proxy purchases and Data API calls are paid from it.

totalSpent.description: Sum of the paid proxy invoices, USD (top-ups excluded).

code.description: Lowercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code: send it as `country`. IPv6 also lists `mix` (any country).

GeoState.description: A state or region. Send `code` as `state` (alias `region`).

country.description: Residential Basic / traffic-based Datacenter: the country asked for.

VideoFrame.description: One storyboard frame: the seek-bar tile closest to a chosen moment. Low resolution (usually 160×90): scenes and objects are visible, small text is not.

n.description: Frame number, matches the `[frame N · m:ss · why]` marker in `content`.

t.description: Second the frame was taken (the storyboard's own grid).

at.description: The same instant as m:ss or h:mm:ss.

reason.description: Why this moment: the speaker points at the screen (cue), a price is said, a chapter starts, the picture changes, or periodic coverage.

quote.description: The words that triggered the frame (cue, price) or the chapter title.

data.description: base64 JPEG. Absent when the request set `frames: false`.

available.description: Every caption track the video offers.

segments.description: The raw timed cues, only when the request set `segments: true`.

chapters.description: The chapters the author wrote in the description (`0:00 Intro`…), in order.

frame_size.description: Size of the frames and the seconds between two storyboard tiles; null when the video has no storyboard (live, very short, or not processed yet).

content.description: The timeline to give the model, in reading order.

full.description: Tokens of the whole timeline before any `max_tokens` trim.

notes.description: What to know about this read: automatic captions, no storyboard, text trimmed to `max_tokens`.

bytes.description: Bytes fetched from the platform (player payload, captions, storyboard sheets).

via_proxy.description: True when the read went through a residential exit after the direct attempt was refused.

RotationResult.description: A restarted sticky session. The next request on the same proxy string gets a new IP.

nextAllowedAt.description: Earliest time this session can rotate again (10 seconds later).

id.description: Link id, used to revoke it.

label.description: Your own name for the link, such as the profile it belongs to.

tokenHint.description: Last 4 characters of the token, to tell links apart.

post.description: Fetches one page through the residential pool and returns it as Markdown, HTML or text. Starts on a TLS-fingerprint tier (fast, cheap) and, with `engine: auto`, escalates to a stealth headless browser only when the target blocks; `render: true` (or `engine: render`, `screenshot`, `xhr`, `reveal_hidden`) forces the browser. Binary documents (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, CSV) are converted to text. Optional structured extraction (`extract` CSS schema or a stored `presetId`) and AI extraction (`ai_prompt`/`ai_schema`) run on the same fetch. Pass `html` instead of `url` to convert markup you already have (no fetch, no proxy bandwidth). What it does not do: it does not solve interactive captchas, and `mode: summary` returns no page content (so it cannot be combined with AI extraction). Billed per successful page by the engine that served it, plus a per-GB bandwidth component with a per-call cap; AI extraction adds the `ai_extract` fee plus marked-up LLM tokens. A page flagged as blocked or a target status ≥ 400 is not charged.

tlsProfile.description: TLS fingerprint profile for the TLS tier (opaque to the API; see /scraper/unlock for the known names).

mode.description: `summary` drops the content and returns only metadata (title, description, canonical, contentLength, engine, bytes) — the light view for audits over many pages.

app_state.description: Mine the page's own hydration state (Next/Nuxt/JSON islands) into `metadata.appState`. `true`/`auto` = pruned to the informative parts; `raw` = full blobs. Alias `appState`.

output.description: Markdown shaping; every key also accepted flat (snake_case) at the top level, flat wins.

404.description: `presetId` does not resolve to one of your presets.

500.description: Extraction failed on our side or timed out (70 s budget). Never billed.

post.description: One search on Google, Bing or DuckDuckGo through the residential pool, returned as JSON in the common SERP-API shape: organic results, ads, People Also Ask, related searches, knowledge panels, AI Overview and 17 Google verticals (`search_type`). `render: true` asks for the rendered Google page (People Also Ask, related questions, ads), `render: false` pins the cheaper HTTP tier, and without `render` the service picks: the HTTP tier for Google web search, a browser for the verticals that need one. Identical requests are served from a 24h cache for free (`search_metadata.from_cache`). It does not paginate on your behalf: request one `page` at a time and read `pagination.available_pages`/`has_next`, or use `/scraper/serp/bulk`. Billed per successful search by the tier that served it (`search_metadata.path`); blocked searches answer 429 and cost nothing; `autocomplete` and `reviews` always bill the request price. Bing: a page whose results answer another query (a decoy) or Bing's "no results" shell is never returned as a result; the service retries as a different browser identity, then once in a real browser, and if nothing genuine comes back the call ends 429 with `code` `bing-decoy` or `bing-no-results`, `attempts` and `retries` (one entry per attempt: `tier`, `outcome`, `reason`) — retry it or use `engine: "google"`. A Bing Success with `organic: []` always carries `search_metadata.empty_reason`.

Every page of one query (`num` above 10, every page of a bulk job) comes from the same device and browser; identities rotate between queries, among current versions and phone models. `search_metadata.served_device` says which page came back (phone or computer layout), `served_platform` and `served_browser` which device and browser fetched it. post.summary: Replay a request through the Web Unlocker
post.description: Send a request the way your own HTTP client would (`url`, `method`, `headers`, `body`) and get it back replayed through a residential or mobile exit under a real browser TLS fingerprint. `mode` decides how far the engine goes: `auto` (default) retries a blocked GET/HEAD/OPTIONS on a fresh exit under a different fingerprint and escalates to a headless browser that answers JavaScript challenges; `tls` never opens the browser; `browser` renders straight away. Any other method gets exactly one attempt (a response means the target saw it, and replaying a POST could double-submit). `format` returns `body` as HTML, Markdown or plain text (`bodyBase64` stays the raw page); `max_bytes` caps what one call may move; `timeout_ms` is the total budget, attempts and render included. `actions` runs clicks, typing, scrolls and waits in the browser before the capture; `cache_ttl` answers a repeated GET from a stored copy, which moves no bytes and costs nothing. A page still blocked after every attempt comes back as 200 with `blocked: true`, `blockClass`, `vendor` and `hint`, never as a silent success; `fail_on_block: true` turns it into 424 `target_blocked`. Every answer carries `request_id`, `latency_ms`, `tier_served`, `attempt_log` and `cost`. When the service has the captcha solver enabled, DataDome and AWS WAF challenges are handed to it; any other interactive captcha is returned as `blockClass: "captcha"`. This is the same engine as the forward proxy (top of this section), without the proxy protocol: no certificate to install; the same call works on `https://app.quanticdata.io/api/v1/scraper/unlock`. Billing is different from every other Data API call: it is metered in bytes against the tier's prepaid Web Unlocker GB (`premium` = residential exits, `mobile` = mobile exits), not the wallet, and every attempt counts (retries, a blocked page, the browser's page load). Errors: one catalogue for the REST call and the proxy, see Unlock errors above. Field names: every camelCase field is also accepted in snake_case (`fail_on_block`, `success_status_codes`, `tls_profile`, `session_id`, `session_duration`, `keep_headers`, `wait_for_selector`, `wait_ms`, `return_cookies`, `auto_render`), and `max_bytes` / `timeout_ms` / `cache_ttl` are also accepted as `maxBytes` / `timeoutMs` / `cacheTtl`. Many URLs at once: `POST /scraper/unlock/batch`.

schema.description: camelCase and snake_case spellings are both accepted for every field (`failOnBlock` / `fail_on_block`, `timeoutMs` / `timeout_ms`, `maxBytes` / `max_bytes`, `successStatusCodes` / `success_status_codes`, `tlsProfile` / `tls_profile`, `sessionId` / `session_id`, `sessionDuration` / `session_duration`, `keepHeaders` / `keep_headers`, `waitForSelector` / `wait_for_selector`, `waitMs` / `wait_ms`, `returnCookies` / `return_cookies`, `autoRender` / `auto_render`, `cacheTtl` / `cache_ttl`). The keys inside an `actions` entry are camelCase only.

url.description: Target URL, `http://` or `https://`. Private, reserved and internal addresses are refused (403 `target_forbidden`); some destinations are not served (403 `target_denied`).

headers.description: Headers your own client would send. Most are replaced by a coherent browser fingerprint (User-Agent, Accept, Sec-Fetch-*); auth, cookie, content-type and custom headers are forwarded verbatim. `keepHeaders: true` forwards everything as-is.

body.description: Request body as UTF-8 text (JSON, form data…). Use this OR `bodyBase64`.

bodyBase64.description: Request body as base64 for binary payloads. Max 8 MB decoded.

tier.description: Which prepaid pool pays and which exits are used. Anything other than `mobile` is `premium`.

mode.description: How far the engine goes. `auto`: TLS tier first, a new exit and fingerprint on each blocked attempt, then the headless browser (it can start in parallel after repeated blocks); `tls`: TLS tier only, never the browser, a blocked page is returned as-is; `browser`: straight to the headless browser (GET/HEAD). The answer says which tier produced it in `tier_served`. Replaces `autoRender` (`mode: "tls"` is the old `autoRender: false`) and `render: "html"` (`mode: "browser"`).

format.description: Format of `body` for HTML responses: the page as HTML, converted to Markdown, or reduced to its text. `bodyBase64` is always the raw page. Ignored when the response is not HTML (JSON, XML, binary); the format served is echoed in `format`.

max_bytes.description: Cap on the bytes this call may move across every attempt (request and response bodies, the browser's page load included). The TLS tier stops downloading past the cap; when the bytes moved exceed it the answer is 403 `max_bytes_exceeded` with `usage` and `cost`: the bytes moved are debited. Also accepted as `maxBytes`.

timeout_ms.description: Total budget of the call in milliseconds: every attempt, the browser render and its settle time fit inside it, never in addition. When it runs out before a response the answer is 504 `timeout`. Also accepted as `timeoutMs`.

fail_on_block.description: `true`: a page still blocked after every attempt answers 424 `target_blocked` (same diagnostics in `payload`) instead of a 200 with `blocked: true`. The GB moved are debited either way. Also accepted as `failOnBlock`.

actions.description: Browser interactions to run, in order, before the page is captured: at most 20. Actions force the browser tier (`tier_served: "browser"`), so they work on GET and HEAD only; together with `mode: "tls"` (or `render: false`, `autoRender: false`) they are refused with 400 `bad_request`. REST only: the proxy has no header for them.

cache_ttl.description: Seconds a usable answer may be served from the cache; 0 is off. A GET the site answered 2xx and that was not blocked is kept for your account for that long. A later call with the same `url`, `mode`, `format`, `country`, `tier`, render kind and `actions` is answered from the copy: `cache: "hit"`, no bytes moved, nothing billed. Also accepted as `cacheTtl`; `x-qp-cache-ttl` on the proxy.

country.description: Exit country, 2-letter code. Without it the exit country is, in order: the site's own country from its ccTLD (`.de`, `.fr`), then the country of your account, then `us`. `customerCountry` / `customer_country` is not a request field: the engine reads the account's country from the account itself.

sessionId.description: Sticky session id — reuse it across calls to keep one exit IP.

mobile.description: Mobile Safari fingerprint (fingerprint only — the product tier is `tier`).

post.description: Starts an asynchronous job of 1 to 100 unlock calls and answers 202 with its `batch_id` at once. Each entry of `requests` is a REST call: `url` plus any field of `POST /scraper/unlock`, `actions` and `cache_ttl` included. `defaults` holds fields applied to every item; an item's own field wins. `urls` is a shorthand for `requests` when the items are plain URLs: send one or the other. post.description: The body is the collector's semantic input exactly as published in its `input_schema` (flat, or wrapped as `{"input": {...}}`), plus runner options: `async: true` forces background processing (also `mode: "async"` or `wait: false`). Short runs answer synchronously with the rows; long ones (the collector decides from the input size) answer 202 with a `statusUrl` to poll. Identical input re-sent inside the dedup window returns the existing run (`deduplicated: true`) — nothing new is created or charged. Per-account brakes (runs per hour, concurrent runs, failure streak) answer 429 with Retry-After. Billed per DELIVERED row at the collector's unit price × your tier discount (some collectors have a small per-run floor, see `price.min_billable_results`); zero rows = zero charge, failed runs are never billed. The worst case (unit × max_results) must be covered by free tier + balance or the run is refused with 402.

post.description: One plain-language prompt → a structured dataset. The service plans queries, searches, maps and scrapes, extracts the requested columns and returns validated rows; `refresh: true` re-reads a known URL set (`refreshUrls`) without discovery at a reduced row fee. post.summary: Generate proxy strings for a plan
post.description: Ready-to-use endpoint strings (credentials included) for one order, in HTTP or SOCKS5 and several formats, with the targeting the plan supports: country/state/city for residential and mobile, ISP code for Residential Premium and Mobile V2 (where state, city and ISP combine in one string), ASN for Residential Basic and traffic-based Datacenter, static gateways for Datacenter. `rotation: sticky` keeps one IP for `sessionTime` minutes; `static` (IPv6 only) is a fixed session with no TTL. Mobile V2 can alternatively return the IP-auth proxy list for a whitelisted `ip`. Premium ISP orders still being provisioned answer 202 with `pending: true`. Premium ISP plans (pool and city) return one line per dedicated IP, each with its own login, and ignore targeting and rotation; `quantity` caps the number of lines (default 10), so pass the plan's `ips` to get every IP. `ipAddresses` holds the exit IP of each line, in the same order as `proxies`. City plans use one port for both HTTP and SOCKS5, and the host of a city line is a connection server that can change: generate the lines again instead of storing the host. The username of each line carries its targeting and session: generate new lines to change them instead of editing the strings by hand. `superSticky: true` keeps one IP per string with no session timer, for as long as the device behind it stays online, on Residential Premium and Mobile; `udp: true` makes Residential Basic SOCKS5 strings relay UDP too. On Residential Basic, `os` picks exit IPs from devices running Windows, Android, iOS or macOS, and `gateway` picks the entry host of the strings in Europe (default), the United States or Asia, for a shorter route from your servers: the exit country still follows `country`. Which parameters apply depends on the plan type: unsupported ones are ignored, not rejected, except `superSticky`, `udp` and `os`, which answer 400 on a plan (or protocol) that cannot honour them; an unknown `os` value, or an unknown `gateway` on Residential Basic, is a 400 too. Free; no Data API billing (the plan's own bandwidth is consumed when you use the proxies).

format.description: `ip:port:user:pass` and the `…@ip:port` spellings are accepted as aliases. On Residential Premium, `http://…` and `socks5://…` lines percent-encode the username and password, so a password that contains `:` or `@` stays intact; the other formats carry them as they are.

state.description: Region slug (Residential Premium / Mobile V2: from the location tree). Alias `region`.

city.description: City slug. On Residential Premium and Mobile V2 a city needs its `state`: without it the city is left out.

sessionTime.description: Sticky session minutes (Residential Basic / Datacenter traffic: min 3 enforced by the gateway).

superSticky.description: Residential Premium and Mobile: a sticky session with no timer, each string keeps its exit IP for as long as the device behind it stays online. It overrides `rotation` and `sessionTime`; the answer's `sessionTime` is `null` on Residential Premium and Mobile V2 (`mobile` plans keep the longest timed session, 1440 minutes). Other plans answer 400 (use `sessionTime` there). Not with the Mobile V2 `ip` flow: whitelist the IP with `sticky: true` and `ttl: 86400` instead.

udp.description: Residential Basic with `protocol: "socks5"`: the strings also relay UDP (SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE), for DNS, QUIC, VoIP and games. Works with rotating and sticky strings on the usual SOCKS5 ports. Your client must support UDP ASSOCIATE and keep the TCP connection it opened for the association open while it sends UDP. Other plans, or `protocol: "http"`, answer 400.

isp.description: ISP code (Residential Premium / Mobile V2, where it combines with `state` and `city` in one string) or carrier ASN (Mobile).

os.description: Residential Basic: exit IPs from devices running this operating system (`mac` is accepted for `macos`). `any`, or no `os`, gives the largest pool. Works with every targeting and with rotating and sticky strings. Other plans answer 400.

filter.description: Residential Premium / Mobile V2 pool filter (default: max pool). It applies to rotating, sticky and super sticky strings alike.

isExtension.description: Rewrite hostnames with a unique prefix so a browser extension cannot cache the proxy (needs the wildcard DNS of the gateway).

ip.description: Mobile V2: a whitelisted IP — returns the IP-auth proxy list instead of user:pass strings.

gateway.description: Mobile V2: region gateway. Residential Basic: entry host of the user:pass strings, `eu` (default; `ww` means `eu`), `us` or `as`. Pick the one closest to where your traffic starts; the exit country still follows `country`, and the same credentials and ports work on all three. Other values answer 400 on Residential Basic.

202.description: Premium ISP order still being provisioned.

example.message: Your dedicated IPs are being prepared. Please check again shortly.

400.description: Missing orderId, expired plan, inactive sub-user, a plan type that cannot generate, `superSticky` / `udp` / `os` on a plan or protocol that does not support them, or an unknown `os` or Residential Basic `gateway` value.

post.summary: Read a YouTube video for a model
post.description: One YouTube URL in; out come the metadata, the transcript in the language that is spoken with `[m:ss]` timestamps (never a translated track: a translation adds the translator's errors on top of the captioner's, and the reading model translates better from the original), the chapters the author wrote, and small storyboard frames picked where the words point at the screen ("as you can see", "come vedete"), where a price is said, at each chapter start and every so often in between, so no stretch goes unseen. `content` interleaves all of it in one Markdown timeline the model reads in order; the frames are base64 JPEGs you attach to the prompt next to their `[frame N]` marker. No model runs on our side. Use `start`/`end` to read a part of a long video and `max_tokens` to bound the text; `max_frames: 0` returns the transcript alone. Reads that the platform refuses from a datacenter address are retried through a residential exit automatically. Pay per success: a video that cannot be read (removed, private, sign-in gated, live not started) answers a stable `payload.code` and is never billed. The MCP server exposes the same call as the `read_video` tool.

url.description: YouTube URL: watch, youtu.be, shorts, embed or live.

languages.description: Caption languages to prefer, e.g. `["en"]`. Leave it out to get the language spoken in the video (recommended: more accurate than a translated track).

frames.description: false = the frame list without image data (positions, reasons and quotes only).

start.description: Read from this point: seconds or `m:ss` / `h:mm:ss`.

end.description: Read up to this point: seconds or `m:ss` / `h:mm:ss`, after `start`.

max_tokens.description: Budget for `content` (estimator chars/4). When the text is trimmed, `tokens.truncated` is true and a note says so: pass `start`/`end` to read the rest.

segments.description: true = also return the raw timed cues under `transcript.segments`.
